and young children&#39;s dietary exposures to lead and cadmium: FDA total diet study 2018-2020</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the quinoa came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-quinoa" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-quinoa-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of quinoa, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FDA Total Diet Study</td><td>3</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for quinoa, cooked on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>FDA Total Diet Study is the only compatible sampling family for quinoa, cooked on this basis in the completed quinoa ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA Total Diet Study</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. The HMI reference for lead in quinoa, as sold pools 27 subgroup units from 2 sampling families, with a median of between 43.8 and 54.5 µg/kg and a middle half spanning below 12.5 (lower quartile) and between 55.8 and 56.4 µg/kg (upper quartile).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bielecka J, Markiewicz-Żukowska R, Puścion-Jakubik A, Grabia M, Nowakowski P, Soroczyńska J, Socha K · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals">Gluten-Free Cereals and Pseudocereals as a Potential Source of Exposure to Toxic Elements among Polish Residents</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nutrients 2022, 14, 2342</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For lead in quinoa, as sold, the reference median was 2.4 µg/kg, with a middle half from 2 to 3.6 µg/kg across 9 units.<sup class="cite">[[sources/hbbf2025-rice-arsenic-cadmium-145-samples|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Houlihan J, Naumoff K · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hbbf2025-rice-arsenic-cadmium-145-samples">What&#39;s in your family&#39;s rice? Arsenic, Cadmium, and Lead in Popular Rice Brands - Plus 9 Safer Grains to Try</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Healthy Babies Bright Futures (HBBF) report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hbbf2025-rice-arsenic-cadmium-145-samples">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium in quinoa, as sold, the reference median was between 29 and 31.5 µg/kg, with a middle half from 22.7 to between 44 and 45 µg/kg across 22 units.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bielecka J, Markiewicz-Żukowska R, Puścion-Jakubik A, Grabia M, Nowakowski P, Soroczyńska J, Socha K · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals">Gluten-Free Cereals and Pseudocereals as a Potential Source of Exposure to Toxic Elements among Polish Residents</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nutrients 2022, 14, 2342</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bielecka2022-poland-gluten-free-cereals-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, quinoa, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in PAHO (29 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (46 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For inorganic arsenic, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (2 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (6.81 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, total arsenic across 30 groups of quinoa ranged from 4 µg/kg (Organic Quinoa (Bolivia and/or Peru)) to 63 µg/kg (Organic Quinoa (Bolivia/Peru)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice Cereals for Infants, Non-Rice Infant Cereal and Other Foods Commonly Eaten by Infants and Toddlers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2016-infant-toddler-foods-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

## Processing, cooking and preparation

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed quinoa in the same study and group. Quinoa, flour or meal (all samples of this type) had lead higher at 550 µg/kg, against 40 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (quinoa, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/roman-ochoa2021-arequipa-grains-health-risk|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Román-Ochoa Y, Choque Delgado GT, Tejada TR, Yucra HR, Durand AE, Hamaker BR · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/roman-ochoa2021-arequipa-grains-health-risk">Heavy metal contamination and health risk assessment in grains and grain-based processed food in Arequipa region of Peru</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemosphere</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/roman-ochoa2021-arequipa-grains-health-risk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.



<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation for quinoa

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>

Lot testing against the applicable limit is the check that can be verified.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No measured way to lower metals in this food is in the library yet.</p>



<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>

Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.
